Uyka the Eavesdropper

Overview

Uyka the Eavesdropper trades in village gossip. She tells Kir stories about Estera, an official and the Remote Mountains, and asks for help repairing a roof. Her later account of Go-Go is explicitly hearsay. She is a source of optional leads and local opinions, not an omniscient narrator. [1, 2]

Uyka’s rumours and the captive Go-Go

Bor introduces Kir to Uyka the Eavesdropper, who lives alone and receives household help in exchange for news. Her first story points toward the giant mushrooms near the goblin camp in the Middle Mountains; only one is edible. Later she reports that a survivor of the Khadaganian expedition left Estera’s refuge for the Distant Mountains. Kir worries that the man might return to Suslanger, and the resulting lead concerns treasure in the ruined expedition camp. Uyka also describes Go-Go as an imprisoned champion of goblin freedom and praises his supposed beauty. Kel is curious enough to consider visiting him, and the pair can free him from the island orcs. Uyka’s requests for repairs, provisions and money accompany these conversations; her account of someone’s motives or attractiveness remains her opinion. [3, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6]

Running bones, the ogre and Uyka’s key

Further paid stories lead Kir to an animated skeleton’s severed legs in the Dead City and to a giant ogre being fattened by the island orcs. The ogre quest proposes overfeeding it: starving it would make it dangerous, while ordinary feeding would let it grow. At the end of this optional sequence, Kir notices the heavy object Uyka wears around her neck. She found it in the mountains and treats it as a possible charm against evil or lizards. Kir recognises it as a key and can buy it. It opens the way to the Hall of the Great in the lizardmen’s tomb, where the greatest chiefs were buried. Among its rewards is another fragment of the Rod of Life, giving Uyka’s local gossip a consequence far beyond Gipath. [7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13]
